I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

I wrote /app/bin/fees.py and ran it on /app/data, which produced /app/out/statements.json. The fee check and the unit tests both pass.

- Unit tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ran 4 tests, all OK.
- Fee check: python tools/check_fees.py matched 228 of 228 statements and 4 of 4 branch rows.

I wrote the script from the rules in /app/docs rather than from the current data, so it should hold for other periods, branches, patrons and calendars. It uses only the standard library. I haven't run it on any input other than /app/data and the four test fixtures.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat docs/overview.md

cd /app/data; cat policy.ini branches.csv; head -20 calendar.csv; head patrons.csv waivers.csv; cat exports/manifest.txt; ls exports | grep -v -E '^[a-z]+-20'; for f in exports/cen-2026-12-15.csv exports/resend-cen.csv exports/har-2027-01-20.jsonl; do head -c 800 $f; echo; done; cat /app/tools/check_fees.py | head -50; sed -n 1,60p /app/tests/test_fees.py
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/fees.py data out/statements.json; echo $?; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30; python tools/check_fees.py

cd /app; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/fees.py following the documented rules and ran it on /app/data to produce /app/out/statements.json. The unit tests pass and check_fees.py reports 228 of 228 statements and 4 of 4 branch rows matching."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
